findings.reason: The protected solution is already the conventional optimal implementation: it rejects unequal lengths, balances aligned characters in one fixed 26-entry array, and accepts exactly when every final count is zero. Its names and structure are concise and interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local and immutable Accepted native sources implement the same length guard, paired character scan, lowercase offset calculation, counter updates, and final all-zero test; only the required LeetCode class-method wrapper differs.

The benchmark now uses legal 256/2,048/16,384-character repeated-letter strings, which force complete scans and expose redundant rescanning. The current source passes at +0.00 relative exponent with a 1.00x largest runtime ratio; a correct implementation that recounts both strings for every character passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.73 with a 12.37x largest runtime ratio.

The Approach now derives the net-balance invariant and zero-vector conclusion explicitly, identifies multiplicity as the semantic trap, treats Unicode as the source follow-up, and no longer describes empty strings outside the stated contract.
The hash-bound modular Reference remains verified against the source structure, including both factual examples, both constraints, and the Unicode follow-up.
